title: Wave-based RBAC v2 migration controller with post-cutover audit validation and SSO mapping harmonizer
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: implement a wave-based migration controller that coordinates incremental RBAC v1->v2 backfills, dual-write consistency checks, and a post-cutover audit validation phase. The controller must minimize customer-visible permission regressions, provide an emergency rollback path, and surface precise audit events (who/when/what changed) to our audit pipeline. This ticket covers orchestration logic, reconciler sampling strategy, backfill throttling, SSO/SAML attribute harmonization, and the streaming audit-forwarder that duplicates RBAC decision events into the new ledger. It also includes comms templates for customers affected by role model differences.
tasks: Design wave controller API: wave definition, window size, eligibility predicates
Implement dual-write middleware that writes to both v1 and v2 with consistent metadata
Build sampling-based reconciler to validate dual-write parity (configurable sample rate)
Implement delta backfill worker with throttling and canary subset support
Add streaming audit-forwarder: emit canonical audit events to audit-s3 + log sink
SSO/SAML attribute harmonizer: deterministic mapping scripts and idempotent transforms
Console: add per-wave progress dashboard and per-customer drift alerts
Emergency rollback hook: automated switch to v1-only for affected customers
End-to-end e2e tests and chaos scenarios (clock skew, partial failures)
Prepare comms bundle: customer notice, FAQ, rollback FAQ, runbook for CSMs
acceptance_criteria: Controller can orchestrate a wave of at least 50 customers and report progress with per-customer reconciliation status
Dual-write achieves >99.9% parity in sampled reconciliation over a 24h window before cutover
Delta backfill can finish a 10M permission record tenant within configured SLA without exceeding DB RPS budget
Audit-forwarder sends canonical events to audit-s3 and the live log sink with end-to-end latency < 10s
SSO mappings are reversible and documented; no SAML customer reports permission misassignment in the canary group
Rollback path executes within defined SLO and restores status without data loss
Automated alerts trigger for drift >0.1% on high-volume tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Shadow waves): run dual-write for 100 small tenants (1% traffic) for 7 days
Phase 1 (Canary): run wave controller on 1% of customers with active monitoring and manual approval
Phase 2 (Batches): escalate to 10% then 50% following parity validation and operational signoff
Phase 3 (Cutover): flip read path to RBAC v2 for migrated waves with audit-validation window of 48h
Phase 4 (Post-cutover): run aggressive backfill for remaining delta and run full-scope reconciliation for 14 days
Emergency rollback: pre-signed runbook triggers immediate read fallback to RBAC v1 for affected waves
monitoring: Per-wave parity metric: ratio of matched decisions to sampled decisions
Backfill throughput and tail latency dashboards
Audit-forwarder success/failure rate and lag histogram
SSO mapping errors and unmapped attributes counter
Automatic health endpoint that verifies dual-write consistency for a control tenant
remediation_plan: If parity < threshold: pause wave controller and triage logs + increase sample rate
If mutation backfill errors: escalate to DB ops and rerun delta job with snapshot isolation
If SSO mapping regression: immediate mapping rollback for affected tenant + manual reconciliation
If audit-forwarder lag > 60s: switch to durable backlog mode and notify SRE
If customer reports permission regression: trigger per-customer rollback and open high-touch support channel
risks: Edge-case permission semantics differ between v1 and v2 leading to functional regressions
Backfill creates DB load spikes causing latency regressions for other services
SSO attribute mismatch for enterprise SAML providers (NameID/email collisions)
Audit duplication or loss during transient failures leading to non-repudiable gaps
Human error during manual approval steps can escalate scope prematurely
